Artists For Kids and the Gordon Smith Gallery of Canadian Art

Address
2121 Lonsdale Avenue
North Vancouver, BC V7M 2K6

Telephone
(604) 903-3798

Email
Artists For Kids: artistsforkids@sd44.ca
Gordon and Marion Smith Foundation: admin@smithfoundation.ca

Office Hours
Monday to Friday 8:30am - 4:30pm
Closed for Statutory Holidays, July and August

Frequently Asked Questions

Are all prints limited edition?

Yes. All prints offered through Artists for Kids are limited editions created in collaboration with Canadian artists and printmakers. The first edition of a limited edition series is archived in the Artists For Kids and the Gordon Smith Gallery Permanent Collection.

Will the artwork look exactly like the images online?

We make every effort to display artwork accurately. However, colours may vary slightly depending on your screen or device.

What payment methods do you accept?

Payments are processed securely through Shopify Payments. Accepted methods may include major credit cards and other options presented at checkout.

How long does shipping take?

Unframed prints are typically shipped within 3–5 business days. Delivery time will depend on your location.

How much is shipping?

Shipping costs are calculated and confirmed at checkout (or during the order process, depending on your location and purchase).

Do you ship framed prints?

Framed prints are available for pickup only. Arranged courier delivery can be arranged at the customer's expense.

Do you offer in-store pickup?

Yes! We offer free in-store pickup.

How long does pickup take?

Unframed prints: ready in 1–2 business days. Framed prints: ready in 2–3 weeks.

We will contact you when your order is ready!

Getting Here

The Gordon Smith Gallery and Artists For Kids is located on the west side of Lonsdale Avenue, across from London Drugs, Steamworks, and Harry Jerome Community Recreation Centre. It is three blocks south from Exit 18 off Trans Canada Hwy 1.

  • Public Transport
    The most convenient way to visit The Gordon Smith Gallery by public transport from downtown Vancouver is via the SeaBus to North Shore’s Lonsdale Quay. From the Terminal, take the 230 or 229 bus towards Upper Lonsdale. This will get you to a stop across the street from the gallery on 21st and Lonsdale. Stop ID: 54200
  • Parking
    One-Hour street parking is available surrounding the Gallery. Pay parking is available on Lonsdale Avenue. There are limited underground parking spaces on P1 and P2, excluding weekends and holidays.

Accessibility

  • The Gordon Smith Gallery and Artists For Kids is wheelchair accessible, with accessible washrooms on the Main level and level 1.
  • There is wheelchair accessible parking on P1 and P2.
  • There is an elevator, accessible through underground parking
  • There is a ramp to the south facing entrance of the building from the street from Lonsdale Avenue.
  • Assistance dogs are welcome. A water bowl is available on request.
  • Please ask our staff if you require any assistance or have any questions.

Music At The Smith is a seasonal concert series dedicated to showcasing highly accomplished musical ensembles across a spectrum of genres, including jazz, folk, indie, classical, and world music. Set within the Gordon Smith Gallery, each performance unfolds alongside the current exhibition featuring Canadian artists. This intersection of disciplines offers the audiences a multi-sensory artistic experience where the visual and auditory arts complement each other. Every ticket purchase directly supports Artists For Kids and the Gordon Smith Gallery programming, ensuring the next generation of creative voices continues to be nurtured and inspired.

The Steinway

The Smith Foundation is honoured to be the proud owner of a 100 year old Steinway & Sons baby grand piano, donated by Kathryn Allison in memory of her mother Barbara Allison, a friend and student of Gordon Smith.

April 2027

This April, Artists For Kids is excited to offer an Artist-in-Residence program for grade 9 students, providing an opportunity to work for two school days at the Artists For Kids studios with artist Mark Johnsen. The Artist-in-Residence programs provide vital skills training and the necessary dedicated time and focus that gives young artists the rare opportunity to immerse themselves in creativity and art making. Selected art students who are nominated by their school will work with professional printmaker, Mark Johnsen.

Mark Johnsen Biography

Mark Johnsen (he/him) is an American visual artist living and working in Vancouver, British Columbia. His print-based practice examines the possibilities of the unique, hand-pulled impression in an era of digital reproduction. Through studies of material exploration, traditional and non-traditional printing techniques: he works to capture gestural and representational time stamps. He is the co-founder of Patio Press, a hybrid printmaking residency run alongside artist, Sara-Jeanne Bourget. He holds a BFA in Photography from California College of the Arts (2012) and an MFA from Emily Carr University of Art + Design (2020). He has exhibited throughout The United States, Canada, The United Kingdom, Turkey, Bosnia, Japan, Switzerland, and New Zealand and is currently an Assistant Professor in Print Media at Emily Carr University of Art + Design.

Mark Johnsen in the Permanent Collection

Past Workshops with Mark Johnsen

February 2024 • Grades 10 to 12

This February, AFK is excited to offer an Artist-in-Residence program for senior art students, providing an opportunity to work for two school days at the AFK studios with artist Mark Johnson. The AFK Artist-in-Residence programs provide vital skills training and the necessary dedicated time and focus that gives young artists the rare opportunity to immerse themselves in creativity and art making. During two school days, senior art students who are nominated by their school will work with professional printmaker, Mark Johnsen.

Each year, Artists For Kids hosts professional development opportunities for K - 12 educators to enhance learning through the lens of the visual arts.

Mark your calendars!

The Gordon and Marion Smith Foundation for Young Artists recognizes the importance of the visual arts as a preservation and expression of culture. We would like to give the opportunity to the next generation of artists, designers, sculptures, painters, etc. to continue following their artistic and creative passion.

The Gordon and Marion Smith Foundation is pleased to offer scholarships to three graduating students from North Vancouver, West Vancouver and Vancouver, who have completed or are enrolled in Grade 12. Applicants must be planning to enrol in an accredited college or university during the upcoming academic year, be in good academic standing and planning to pursue an arts-related major or minor in Canada.

As part of applying, applicants must submit a digital portfolio of their work.

North Vancouver

The $2,500 Gordon and Marion Smith Foundation North Vancouver Young Artist Scholarship is available to a graduating student, enrolled in a public or private North Vancouver school, who has demonstrated excellence in the Visual Arts and is planning to continue their education in the Visual Arts in Canada (visual arts include traditional media as well as photographic and digital media).

West Vancouver

The $2,500 Gordon and Marion Smith Foundation West Vancouver Young Artist Scholarship is available to a graduating student, enrolled in a public or private West Vancouver school, who has demonstrated excellence in the Visual Arts and is planning to continue their education in the Visual Arts in Canada (visual arts include traditional media as well as photographic and digital media).

Vancouver

The $2,500 Gordon and Marion Smith Foundation Vancouver Young Artist Scholarship is available to a graduating student, enrolled in a public or private Vancouver school, who has demonstrated excellence in the Visual Arts and is planning to continue their education in the Visual Arts in Canada (visual arts include traditional media as well as photographic and digital media).

For Artists For Kids Scholarships (separate from Gordon and Marion Smith Foundation Scholarships) Please visit: Artists For Kids Scholarships

The Brilliance Gala is a chance to come together to support a key facet of Gordon Smith’s legacy: quality, artist- and educator-led arts education for children and youth across the Lower Mainland through Artists for Kids. As public funding becomes increasingly constrained, your support helps safeguard long-term sustainability by protecting the specialized people, tools, and learning environments that make high-quality arts education possible.

Brilliance Gala 2026

Thank you for joining us for a wonderful evening on Wednesday March 11th, 2026! The Gordon And Marion Smith Foundation is incredibly grateful for your contributions to the success of Brilliance Gala 2026.

Together with Co-Chairs Ian Wallace (O.C) and Krista Whitelock, our wonderful community of friends, artists, gallerists, donors, bidders, volunteers and more came together to raise $250,000, supporting the next generation of young artists at Artists For Kids and the Gordon Smith Gallery. Hosted by Fred Lee and Gloria Macarenko, guests enjoyed an evening of fine dining by Chef David Hawksworth, entertainment and a Live and Online Auction of a selection of curated artworks by Canadian artists, unique and luxury items, and one-of-a-kind experience packages.

Co-Chairs: Ian Wallace (O.C) and Krista Whitelock

Committee: John David James, Christos Dikeakos, Allison Kerr, Hilary Letwin, Alexandra Pony, Tyler Quarles, Richard Savage, Ed Tsumura, Dr. Anne Watt, and Bruce Munro Wright (O.B.C)

Photography by Jamie Lee Fuoco

The Gala at Camp Smith

Together with returning Brilliance co-chairs Ian Wallace and Patti Glass, we gathered on March 12, 2025 to celebrate the 30th anniversary of the Artists For Kids Paradise Valley Summer School for the Visual Arts, and raised $228,000 to support the next generation of young artists.

Hosted by Fred Lee and Gloria Macarenko, guests enjoyed an evening of fine dining by Chef David Hawksworth and live entertainment at The Gordon Smith Gallery of Canadian Art.

The Gala at Camp Smith included a Live and Online Auction featuring a curated selection of artworks, luxury items and one-of-a-kind experience packages.

Photography by When They Find Us

Brilliance 2023

In Tribute to the Life and Legacy of Gordon Smith

Together with Brilliance co-chairs Yoshi Karasawa, Ian Wallace and Patti Glass, we gathered on June 15, 2023 to celebrate the enduring legacy of Gordon Smith while supporting the cause closest to his heart: exceptional art education for all.

Hosted by Vicki Gabereau and Fred Lee, guests enjoyed an evening of fine dining, entertainment and special tributes to Gordon Smith at the scenic Pipe Shop Venue at the North Vancouver Shipyards.

Brilliance featured a unique auction format: a limited Live Auction featuring one piece from each of the Artists for Kids Founding Artist Patrons: Gordon Smith, Jack Shadbolt and Bill Reid. Select experience packages were also curated with Gordon Smith's love of art, modernist architecture, and the natural world in mind.

The Friends of Gordon Collection

The primary focus of the evening was the extensive Friends of Gordon Collection, a new collection of over 50 artworks that serve as a remarkable testament to the exchange of creativity that Gordon Smith fostered among his peers, as well as those he met throughout his life. The artists represented each contributed an artwork that pays homage to Gordon Smith in some form, whether it be through direct creative kinship and mentorship, or by having worked closely with the Smith Foundation and Artists for Kids. The collection spans a wide range of artistic styles, valuation, and recognition - all with one purpose of showing the vast impact that Gordon had on so many.

Guests: 300. Raised: $471,000.

View the Catalogue

Spring Luncheons

16th Annual Spring Luncheon, June 2, 2019

Guests: 150. Raised: $148,000.

2019 auction catalogue (PDF)

Off the Wall: A Fundraiser with a Twist

Each year, fifteen of Vancouver’s most respected collectors donate an original work to the Smith Foundation. These works are then sold at a by-invitation-only auction held at Hawksworth Restaurant’s York Room at the Rosewood Hotel Georgia. All funds raised are directed to the Smith Foundation in support of its ongoing efforts to enhance art education in our community.

Artists for Kids is grateful for the generosity and commitment of the Canadian artists who have worked directly with children and youth through the many Artist for Kids' educational programs and who have gifted work to the Artists for Kids Limited Edition Portfolio for over 37 years.

The Artists for Kids Limited Edition program releases Seasonal Portfolios of artworks for acquisition. The releases feature limited editions of both new and existing artist collaborators.

Artists for Kids was founded in 1989 with the singular intent to support art education, for all.

In 1989, the founders of AFK sought to find a financial model to support arts education in our schools, one that was sustainable, and in turn, would support visual arts enrichment. By purchasing art from artists, then in turn inviting each artist to create original, limited-edition prints that the program could sell, the founders created a unique and lasting fundraising vehicle. With the generosity, commitment and support of founding artist-patrons Gordon Smith, Jack Shadbolt and Bill Reid, Artists for Kids was born, and with it, the acclaimed Artist for Kids and Gordon Smith Gallery Permanent Collection of Canadian Art.

Thanks to the ongoing support of our community, artist-patrons, and the North Vancouver School District, Artist for Kids has grown from an idea onto a world-class art program.

Through art specialists, Artists for Kids provides enriching art-making experiences for thousands of students each year across Canada, as well as professional development opportunities for educators.

In 1990, with the support of art educators and artist patrons Bill Reid, Jack Shadbolt, and Gordon Smith, the first Artists for Kids Limited Edition Portfolio print, Xhuwaji / Haida Grizzly was published - marking the beginning of an extraordinary partnership between Canadian artists and Artists for Kids.

Entering its 37th year, Artists for Kids continues to work with renowned Canadian artists and print studios across Canada to publish contemporary limited editions; its portfolio is now revered as one of the most significant limited edition collections in Canada.

The Artists for Kids Limited Edition Portfolio program funds educational programs, artist residencies, art camps, scholarships, bursaries, and future acquisitions for the Artists for Kids and the Gordon Smith Gallery Permanent Collection.

Artists for Kids was established in 1989 by tenacious educators and renowned B.C. artists Gordon Smith, Jack Shadbolt, and Bill Reid. Supported by the North Vancouver School District, it was founded with the singular intent to support children, their art education, and their future.

Through art specialists, Artists for Kids provides enriching art-making experiences for thousands of students annually, as well as professional development opportunities for educators.

In 1990, the program published the first Artists for Kids’ Limited Edition Portfolio print, Xhuwaji / Haida Grizzly. This print by Bill Reid, based on a ceremonial drum, marked the beginning of an extraordinary partnership with now more than 100 Canadian artists, which has produced one of the most significant limited edition collections in the country. 

Acquiring a limited edition print by renowned Canadian artists funds our educational programs, artist residencies, art camps, scholarships, bursaries, and future acquisitions for Artists for Kids and the Gordon Smith Gallery Permanent Collection, directly supporting the future of children and youth.

before.body:
Gordon Appelbe Smith, CM, OBC, LLD, June 18, 1919 – January 18, 2020, is a cornerstone in the history of Modernist painting in Canada. His works are held in the collections of the National Gallery of Canada, the Vancouver Art Gallery, the Museum of Modern Art in New York, and the Victoria and Albert Museum in London, England, among others. Gordon’s deep belief in art education is what grounds our organization, and what has touched the lives of so many young Canadians.

The consummate artist, educator and art patron, Smith actively supported local visual art initiatives, mentored many, and spent hours a day in the studio. His body of work, executed in many different media, encompasses a diverse range of interests including his displacement to Canada from England as a young man; his World War II experiences; the natural beauty of the British Columbia landscape; and the tension between abstraction and representation.

He believed that creativity was essential to everything, and, in order to be the best we can be at whatever it is that we do, it needs to be fostered.

His late wife, Marion Smith was said to have two careers, one as a celebrated social worker and another as Gordon’s boss. She possessed a keen eye for art and was a great influence on Gordon’s work. Her career in Social Services was buoyed by her belief that support for the arts creates healthy communities.

Together, their tireless work and dedication over the course of 50 years influenced the progression of Canadian art and helped to shape the lives of thousands of young people and emerging and established artists.

It is our great honour and fervent intent to foster their legacy as we continue to support Gordon Smith's vision to develop a love of the arts in our communities.

You can read his obituary in the Globe & Mail and the Vancouver Sun. Listen to Smith Foundation Board Chair, Paul Killeen speak about Gordon on The Early Edition on CBC.

before.body:
Frequently Asked Questions

Are all prints limited edition?

Yes. All prints offered through Artists for Kids are limited editions created in collaboration with Canadian artists and printmakers. The first edition of a limited edition series is archived in the Artists for Kids and the Gordon Smith Gallery Permanent Collection.

Will the artwork look exactly like the images online?

We make every effort to display artwork accurately. However, colours may vary slightly depending on your screen or device.

What payment methods do you accept?

Payments are processed securely through Shopify Payments. Accepted methods may include major credit cards and other options presented at checkout.

How long does shipping take?

Unframed prints are typically shipped within 3–5 business days. Delivery time will depend on your location.

How much is shipping?

Shipping is a flat rate of $20 within Canada.

Do you ship outside Canada?

Not at this time. We ship within Canada only.

Do you ship framed prints?

Framed prints are available for pickup only. Arranged courier delivery can be arranged at the customer's expense.

Do you offer in-store pickup?

Yes! We offer free in-store pickup.

How long does pickup take?

Unframed prints: ready in 1–2 business days. Framed prints: ready in 2–3 weeks.

We will contact you when your order is ready!
